title: The Full Inbox Reconciliation
description: Walk one shipment through its entire life — booked, paid, delivered — and reconcile exactly what should exist in both the in-app notification center and the mock outbox against what actually got written, leaving nothing to assumption.
successCondition: As one customer: book a shipment, create and pay its invoice successfully, then advance the shipment to delivered. After waiting past the queue delay for the last event, querying the DB via `npm run db:psql`: the notifications table has exactly 3 new rows for this user (types shipment.booked, payment.succeeded, shipment.delivered, in that chronological order by created_at), and the mock_messages table has exactly 4 new rows (email for shipment.booked, email for payment.succeeded, email AND sms for shipment.delivered) — confirm the exact 3-and-4 counts and every row's type/channel, not just that "some" rows exist.
hints: The trigger -> type -> title -> channel table in docs/api/notifications.md tells you exactly which events send which channels — shipment.delivered is the only one of the three sending on both.
Scope every count query to this specific user's id/email — the seeded demo data and other test runs will have unrelated rows in both tables that would otherwise pollute your counts.
